motto: Serving Greywater Falls since 1887, and the lake somewhat longer.
weather: Overcast, mild, 38°F, fog lying thick on the water past noon and slow to lift

undercurrent.phenomenon: A fifth cup has been set at The Kettle without instruction, filled overnight, accompanied by a place card in an unrecognized hand bearing a name Marigold will not disclose; simultaneously the library's card, now locked away, gains a sixteenth stamp despite the box remaining unopened and unkeyed, meaning the season's central object has begun producing effects at a distance from its own physical containment, decoupling the phenomenon from the object entirely.
undercurrent.note: Good compounding beat: containment (Calloway's lockbox) has failed to stop the stamping, which raises the stakes past 'the card moves' into 'the card's effect no longer needs the card present.' Marigold naming a guest without naming them to the reader keeps the reader hungry without forcing reveal. Doreen's lost hour has now escalated from forty minutes to roughly sixty, and should tip toward a stated cause or a direct confrontation with Agnes/Wren within the next few days rather than repeat the same beat a third time. Agnes's held half-riddle for Wren is now overdue for release; consider delivering it within 2-3 days to keep pace with the crest. The fifth place setting all but names the shape of who fills it: do not answer that outright yet, but the next natural beat is either the place card's name leaking, or the fifth chair being physically occupied at dusk.

editor.name: Wren Aldercott
editor.voice: Dry, precise, allergic to drama, which is unfortunate given recent events. Writes like a person holding a clipboard while standing in rising water. Lets one true thing slip per edition, usually in the last line.

season_arc.premise: Calloway finishes reshelving the east alcove in the last cataloguer's 2009 order and finds, tucked behind where the ninth book sat, a library card checked out that same interrupted Wednesday and never returned. It is due back today. The borrower's name is nobody currently living in Greywater Falls has ever heard of, and the little pocket calendar stamped inside has fourteen years of due-date stamps on it already, one for every year since, each in a different hand.
